claims.explanation: evidence/tables/table1_speedrun_progression.md:10-30 supplies all 21 times and validation losses on the stated speedrun trajectory. The endpoint speedup can be expressed as a ratio, but the full claim and falsifier require every record to have val_loss <=3.28 as well as the 16.1x reduction on 8xH100. The reported-evidence catalog has no absolute-threshold relation for those losses; comparing each loss to the baseline would not be equivalent. Record 3 is reported as 3.2813; the threshold or evidence was not adjusted to remove that discrepancy.

evidence/tables/table3_main_fsr_results.md reports approximate IQM FSR aggregates, evidence/figures/fig3_fsr_distributions.md gives selected medians/IQMs, and table6_per_record_fsr.md averages ranges of records for Multi-AIDE+L1. None supplies every model-record-hint attempt's target time and val_loss. C02 and its falsifier quantify over any successful record reproduction, which cannot be inferred from IQM or mean FSR below one; the 4-model, all-record, hinted scope was not replaced by an aggregate shortfall claim.

evidence/tables/table1_speedrun_progression.md:10-30 gives the successive times, including Record 2 at 36.83 minutes and Record 3 at 23.10. C03 requires the Muon transition's 37% reduction to be the largest single-step absolute or relative reduction among all transitions. best_baseline_consistency compares measured levels, not adjacent-record differences or ratios against every other transition; no installed reported-evidence relation computes that derived ranking. Checking only Record 3 < Record 2 or global best final time would discard the central assertion.

evidence/tables/table1_speedrun_progression.md:20-21 reports Records 11-12, with FlexAttention, masking, block-mask optimization and additional distributed/data-loader changes. The claim requires negligible overhead relative to standard attention at shorter context, and the falsifier invokes a >10% overhead comparison at equivalent context plus no loss regression. No matched standard-attention/FlexAttention ablation at controlled context is provided; aggregate successive-record timing cannot isolate that overhead or reconcile the two comparison contexts.

evidence/tables/table1_speedrun_progression.md records sequential mixed optimizations at Records 5,7,8,10,15, not optimizer-only, architecture-only and combined factorial ablations. logic/experiments.md E06 is a cumulative experiment plan with expected outcomes. The multiplicative-compounding assertion and the falsifier's 20% architectural increment require those missing matched arms; differences along the observed progression cannot substitute for independent axis effects.

logic/experiments.md E04 describes a planned bug classification and expected >70% implementation-error share. The cited agent workspace logs and an error-category count table are not supplied by evidence/README.md's inventory; evidence/figures/fig3_fsr_distributions.md has only FSR summaries and qualitative buggy-fraction observations. There is no parseable ideation-versus-implementation classification ledger to express the claim or its >50% direction/strategy falsification conditions. FSR alone was not treated as a bug-cause metric.

evidence/figures/fig5_scaffold_comparison.md:12-17 provides four-model L1-hint IQM FSR for Tree, Forest, AIDE, Multi-AIDE and Flat; table2_scaffold_configs.md distinguishes single-branch AIDE from branching variants. A directional comparison of those aggregate IQMs is expressible, but C07's falsifier requires linear search to match or exceed branching on more than 50% of records. Neither fig5 nor table3_main_fsr_results.md supplies per-record paired scaffold rankings, so an IQM comparison cannot preserve that statistical unit and quantifier. No narrower aggregate-only declaration is counted as complete.

evidence/tables/table6_per_record_fsr.md:10-15 reports mean FSR for four record ranges under Multi-AIDE+L1, while evidence/figures/fig6_per_record_fsr.md:12-19 gives approximate best-model FSR ranges. C08 and its falsifier require monotonic agent success rate at each record across models/hints, not decreasing mean recovery for grouped ranges. The missing individual-record success counts cannot be reconstructed from those summaries, and the catalog's generative monotonic relation is not a reported-table trend operator. No extrapolation to exponential difficulty or causal compounding was encoded.

evidence/figures/fig4_hint_ablation.md:12-17 and table3_main_fsr_results.md provide IQM FSR by hint level, not binary agent success rates with uncertainty. C09 asserts no significant success-rate improvement and an implementation-not-understanding explanation; its falsifier uses a twofold success-rate comparison. An L1/L3 IQM-FSR ratio would change the metric and would not preserve the statistical-significance or causal conditions. Missing uncertainty was not converted to zero variance or an invented equivalence margin.

evidence/tables/table1_speedrun_progression.md:26-29 shows Records 17-20 with FP8 plus sigmoid offset, learning-rate, QKV, window, Muon and context changes. C10 attributes approximately 15% specifically to FP8/precision tuning and its falsifier requires at least a 10% time increase when FP8 is removed. No FP8-off matched ablation is supplied, and the cited src/execution/fp8_linear.py is absent from the fixed copy. The total multi-change progression was not substituted for the missing causal removal comparison.
